commits.author: Lasse Tyrihjell
commits.message:
Masking oauth2- and custom header values when logging outgoing requests

The log-endpoints in the subscription-routes use showAll=true, which renders the
complete header-map. Since they are placed after addCustomHeaders() and after
direct:oauth2.authorize, every subscription start, check-status, cancel and data
request wrote the customHeaders of the data provider and the Authorization-header
to the log at INFO.

Requests that may carry credentials are now logged through a formatter that masks
the values of the oauth2-headers, Authorization and every header name configured
as a customHeader on any subscription. The key is still logged, so it remains
visible that the header was applied.

Note that the log-component has no uri-option for supplying a formatter, and an
endpoint resolved through the CamelContext is already initialized - hence the
endpoint is constructed directly.

commits.author: Lasse Tyrihjell
commits.message:
Comparing customHeaders and oauth2Config when detecting updated subscriptions

Both change the outgoing request, so a difference in either is exactly the
updated subscription-config equals() is meant to detect. Without this, a pod
holding a correct config discarded it in favour of a stale copy already in
Hazelcast, and no redeploy could fix it.

Treating null and empty as equivalent to avoid flagging already registered
subscriptions as updated. Logging the differing keys only - the values are
credentials.

commits.author: Lasse Tyrihjell
commits.message:
Failing startup on unresolved placeholders in subscription-config

Spring binds an unresolvable ${...} as the literal string, so a secret that was
not available when the config was bound is sent to the data provider as-is -
looking like an auth-failure at the far end, with no signal on our side.

Checking customHeaders, oauth2Config and urlMap in isValid. Only the offending
key is logged - the value may be a secret.

commits.author: Lasse Tyrihjell
commits.message:
Harden XML parsing against XXE in SiriXmlValidator

Inbound SIRI-XML from external providers was parsed with the permissive
JDK defaults (XMLInputFactory/DocumentBuilderFactory), allowing external
entity resolution and DTD-based attacks (XXE / billion laughs).

Add SecureXmlFactories with DTD and external entities disabled, and use
it for both the StAX and DOM parsers in SiriXmlValidator.

Verified with SecureXmlFactoriesTest: the previous DocumentBuilder
actually attempted to read file:///etc/hostname; the hardened factory
now rejects the DOCTYPE while still parsing valid SIRI.

commits.author: Lasse Tyrihjell
commits.message:
Add SIRI Validation landing page listing all codespaces

New GET /anshar/validation endpoint renders a responsive Bootstrap card
grid (up to 4 columns) with one card per codespace and its subscription
count. Cards are clickable into the existing per-codespace validation
page; that page gains a back-link to the landing page.

Implementation:
- SubscriptionManager.getCodespaces() aggregates subscriptions by
  case-insensitive codespace, skipping null/blank dataset ids, and
  picks the alphabetically smallest variant per group for deterministic
  display (Hazelcast IMap iteration order is not insertion-ordered).
- New Camel route direct:validation.index renders templates/validation-index.ftl
- Unit test in SubscriptionManagerTest covers grouping, counting,
  sorting and the null/blank filter.
